srf_frame_fixed_truepos_geocentric.description: SRF v1.0 Dhruva Chitra frame-fixed profile: user-defined sidereal mode frozen at J2000 on the J2000 ecliptic (SIDBIT_ECL_T0), geometric TRUEPOS planets, TRUE_NODE nodes.
srf_frame_fixed_truepos_geocentric.ayanamsa_method_note: Verified live 2026-07-08: swe.get_ayanamsa_ex_ut() does not correctly honor SIDBIT_ECL_T0's frozen reference (it returns a nutation/date-dependent value regardless of flags, off by several to ~17 arcsec depending on epoch); the flags-less swe.get_ayanamsa_ut() computes it correctly for this sidereal mode. Every other profile in this file is unaffected (they use plain SIDM_TRUE_CITRA or a legacy mode, not SIDBIT_ECL_T0) and keeps get_ayanamsa_ex_ut.

DPL.name: DPL
DPL.description: Kaalam/JHora-compatible DPL profile: True Chitra/Spica anchor, geometric TRUEPOS planet flags, and TRUE_NODE for Rahu/Ketu. Use this when matching DPL/JHora-style geometric calculations.
DPL.scientific_note: This is a coherent geometric calculation profile, not proof that one astrological interpretation is scientifically predictive. Apparent and TRUEPOS positions are both astronomically valid but answer different coordinate-model questions. DPL deliberately uses the TRUEPOS (true geometric) frame for planets, house cusps, and the displayed ayanamsa so all three share one internally consistent sidereal reference.

custom_params.zero_epoch_description: Verified property, NOT a computation input. The instant when the live DPL/TRUE_CITRA truepos ayanamsa equals 0° — equivalently, when Spica sits at exactly 180.000000° sidereal. Computed by bisection against the actual implementation; the runtime never references this value (Swiss TRUE_CITRA is self-anchoring).
custom_params.calculation_method: Uses Swiss Ephemeris TRUE_CITRA (mode 27) with SEFLG_SIDEREAL | SEFLG_TRUEPOS | SEFLG_SPEED for planets and TRUE_NODE for Rahu/Ketu. House cusps use the same SEFLG_TRUEPOS sidereal frame so cusps and grahas never drift apart.
accuracy_features: True geometric (SEFLG_TRUEPOS) positions: light-time, annual aberration, and gravitational light-deflection are intentionally EXCLUDED so the sidereal reference stays stable
Spica proper motion accounted for via Swiss TRUE_CITRA (~43 milliarcseconds/year)
Nutation retained in the sidereal frame (IAU 2000/2006 precession-nutation)
Ayanamsa annual wobble is only ~±1.5 arcsec (pure nutation), versus ~±21 arcsec for the apparent-frame True Chitra profile (Spica's annual aberration)
Planets, house cusps, and the displayed ayanamsa all share one truepos frame (internally consistent to <1e-6 deg)
Optional JPL DE440/DE441 backend for sub-milliarcsecond ephemeris
custom_params.accuracy_claim: DPL is the explicit TRUEPOS/JHora-compatible True Chitra profile, computed directly from Swiss/JPL TRUE_CITRA. It is geometrically rigorous and internally consistent across grahas, cusps, and ayanamsa; it is not a scientific proof of predictive astrology.

True Chitra Astrometric.name: True Chitra Astrometric
True Chitra Astrometric.description: Research profile: True Chitra/Spica anchor in the astrometric frame — light-time retained, annual aberration and gravitational deflection removed. This is the rigorous 'observed' sidereal place of a body against the real star field, complementary to the default geometric DPL. Opt-in; not the default.
True Chitra Astrometric.scientific_note: Astrometric = where a body is actually seen among the fixed stars: its true geometric direction corrected for light-time (the body's motion during light travel), with the observer-velocity aberration and relativistic light-deflection removed because those displace the apparent image without representing the body's place in the zodiac. Differs from the default geometric DPL by each body's light-time (Sun ~0, Moon ~15 arcsec, Mercury up to ~40 arcsec). Use DPL for classical/JHora-compatible geometric positions; use this to compare against the modern observed astrometric place.

custom_params.calculation_method: Swiss Ephemeris TRUE_CITRA (mode 27) with SEFLG_SIDEREAL | SEFLG_NOABERR | SEFLG_NOGDEFL | SEFLG_SPEED for planets and TRUE_NODE for Rahu/Ketu; house cusps and the displayed ayanamsa use the matching SEFLG_NOABERR | SEFLG_NOGDEFL frame.

Dhruva Chitra.name: Dhruva Chitra
Dhruva Chitra.description: Frame-fixed sidereal zodiac: Spica's measured J2000 direction frozen at 180 degrees forever in the inertial ICRS frame, measured on the fixed J2000 ecliptic. The first kinematically non-rotating ayanamsa in Kaalam -- the zodiac never rotates with the star's proper motion (unlike True Chitra/DPL) and is defined by published conventional constants (IAU-style: an epoch and an angle), not a fitted table or a tracked star.
Dhruva Chitra.reference_star: Spica (alpha Virginis) - direction frozen at J2000.0

custom_params.sid_mode_note: swisseph_code 511 = SIDM_USER(255) | SIDBIT_ECL_T0(256); reference_jd is TT

Dhruva Chitra.scientific_note: Definition/realization discipline: (reference_jd, ayanamsa_at_reference) IS the frame -- exact by convention, like the meter or ICRS -- not a fitted approximation. Verified live (2026-07-08): this Theta0 cross-checks to 0.0125 arcsec between an independent Hipparcos-2/ERFA computation and Swiss Ephemeris's own SIDM_USER|SIDBIT_ECL_T0 reconciliation (gate <0.1 arcsec). It differs from DPL's ayanamsa at J2000 by ~13.93 arcsec -- measured and attributed to nutation-in-longitude (DPL's TRUEPOS/SIDM_TRUE_CITRA path does not exclude nutation; Dhruva Chitra's SIDBIT_ECL_T0 path was verified to always operate on mean, non-nutated elements regardless of caller flags), not a catalog error. See docs/audit/srf-v1-derivation/derivation_report.md for the full derivation, citations, and this root-cause analysis.
Dhruva Chitra.accuracy_note: Realized zero point uncertainty ~0.005 arcsec (Hipparcos-2 realization budget); exact by convention thereafter. Unlike every star-tracking ayanamsa (True Chitra, True Revati, True Pushya, ...), Spica's own sidereal longitude under this system drifts away from 180 degrees over time at its own proper-motion rate (~-0.028 arcsec/year, verified) -- this is the direct, single-star signature that the frame is fixed rather than tracking.

lahiri_zero_epoch_discovery.finding: Through ultra-high precision search, we discovered that the Lahiri ayanamsa equals exactly 0° at September 2, 285 CE, 13:43:34.184761 UTC (JD 1825399.071923434734). This is the exact zero crossing point where the Lahiri ayanamsa transitions from 359.999...° to 0.000...°. This is 5.63 years before KSK's 291 CE reference.
lahiri_zero_epoch_discovery.conclusion: Any zero-epoch-based ayanamsa using Lahiri as baseline would be mathematically identical to Lahiri itself.

dpl_ayanamsa_discovery.finding: TRUE_CITRA (Swiss Ephemeris mode 27) anchors the sidereal frame to Spica/Citra. Kaalam models this through explicit position profiles: apparent geocentric for general True Chitrapaksha and TRUEPOS geometric for DPL/JHora compatibility. The DPL runtime delegates entirely to Swiss TRUE_CITRA; it does NOT perform any zero-epoch anchoring or year-by-year precession integration.

zero_epoch.meaning: Verified property of the live implementation (not a computation input): the instant when DPL/TRUE_CITRA truepos ayanamsa = 0°, i.e. Spica at exactly 180.000000° sidereal. Computed by bisection against the actual engine.
zero_epoch.correction_note: Supersedes two earlier, mutually inconsistent and incorrect values (JD 1825184.474 / Jan 30 285 CE in config, and JD 1825390.36 / Aug 24 285 CE in the docs). The live DPL ayanamsa is -13.6 arcsec at the former and +11.0 arcsec at the latter, so neither was the true zero.

accuracy_comparison.DPL_profile: Uses TRUE_CITRA with SEFLG_TRUEPOS for geometric/JHora-compatible calculations of planets AND house cusps (one shared frame).
accuracy_comparison.True_Chitrapaksha_profile: Uses TRUE_CITRA without SEFLG_TRUEPOS for apparent geocentric calculations; its ayanamsa carries a ~±21 arcsec annual aberration wobble that DPL does not.
accuracy_comparison.TRUE_NODE_vs_MEAN_NODE: TRUE_NODE and MEAN_NODE are different lunar node models; Kaalam DPL keeps TRUE_NODE for Rahu/Ketu.
